title: Portrait and Cellar
premise: Mirabel Sterling, a meticulous property surveyor who has spent his life keeping himself unremarkable, is hired to appraise Hollowmere House before its demolition. When an excavation crew unearths a cellar door sealed from the inside—dated 1974—the house begins counting him back: doors that appear where none were, portraits whose eyes track him, and a ledger bearing his own handwriting in ink he never bought. He learns the house was built over a foundling home whose children were 'appraised' by something beneath it, and that in 1974 a caretaker named Odile Voss stole its ledger to free them, sealing herself and her charges inside rather than surrender them. To end the haunting—and save the excavation crew it has begun claiming—Mirabel must return the ledger, but returning it means offering the house a new keeper. In the climax he refuses to give himself and instead gives the house what it truly wanted: recognition, reading every child's name aloud until the cellar door opens from the inside at last. The house releases him, Odile's portrait finally smiles, and Mirabel walks out changed—visible, named, and no longer alone.
about_author: Ines Amberdale is the pen name of a former building inspector who spent fifteen years cataloguing condemned properties across the English coast. Their fiction explores the quiet horror of structures that remember more than the people who live in them.

chapters.title: The Man Who Measures
chapters.summary: Mirabel Sterling's POV. We meet him mid-survey of a derelict pub, establishing his rituals: count doors, keep lights on, stay invisible. His firm assigns him Hollowmere House, a job no one else wants. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: Hollowmere at First Light
chapters.summary: Mirabel arrives at the estate, a Georgian pile slated for demolition. The house is wrong in small ways—forty-one doors where plans show forty. He logs it as surveyor's error. Beat: unease rationalized away.

chapters.title: The Portrait That Wasn't There Yesterday
chapters.summary: In the east hall hangs a portrait of a stern woman in caretaker's clothes, unlabeled. Mirabel checks his own photos from day one; the wall was bare. Beat: first undeniable anomaly, met with stubborn documentation.

chapters.title: Crew of Six
chapters.summary: POV shifts briefly to Danny Okafor, excavation foreman, whose crew arrives to break ground on the annex. Danny likes Mirabel's fussiness; the crew teases him gently. Beat: first flicker of belonging Mirabel doesn't know how to accept.

chapters.title: Lights On, Doors Counted
chapters.summary: Mirabel's night routine at the site trailer. A light burns in an upstairs window of the empty house. He counts doors from outside: forty-two now. Beat: dread compounding; his rules are failing.

chapters.title: Ground Penetrating
chapters.summary: Danny's crew hits a void under the west lawn. Ground radar shows a rectangular chamber, pre-dating the house. The client wants it ignored; Danny wants it opened. Beat: duty versus curiosity.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Wall
chapters.summary: Mirabel finds a cavity behind the portrait containing a leather ledger, water-stained, dated 1974. Inside are children's names with columns: 'kept,' 'fed,' 'taken.' The last entry is in handwriting identical to his own. Beat: personal violation.

chapters.title: Sealed From the Inside
chapters.summary: The crew excavates a stone door set into the cellar's outer wall—bolted shut from within, hinges green with fifty years. Scratched into the stone: DON'T OPEN FOR US. Beat: the invitation that is also a warning.

chapters.title: Odile Voss, Caretaker
chapters.summary: Mirabel researches archives: Odile Voss ran Hollowmere's foundling home until 1974, when she and eleven children vanished the night of a fire that never burned. The portrait is her. Beat: grief for a stranger.

chapters.title: What the House Wants
chapters.summary: The house begins responding to Mirabel—doors opening to rooms he needs, the ledger appearing on his pillow. It isn't haunting him; it's courting him. Beat: seduction of being needed.

chapters.title: Danny's Dream
chapters.summary: Danny POV. He dreams of a woman counting children against a cellar wall, waking with tally marks scratched on his forearm. The crew jokes; Danny doesn't. Beat: the house widening its reach.

chapters.title: Forty-Three
chapters.summary: Mirabel counts forty-three doors. Behind the newest one: a child's bedroom, dust-free, bed warm. A name carved in the headboard: PIP. Beat: terror braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: The Appraisal
chapters.summary: Mirabel submits his report; the client demands he certify the void as 'no significant finding.' His career, his invisibility, offered back if he lies. Beat: love against duty begins—duty says sign.

chapters.title: Taken
chapters.summary: A crew member, Reyes, goes missing during a solo shift. Found hours later at the sealed door, unharmed, repeating names he shouldn't know. Beat: stakes turn physical.

chapters.title: Reading the Ledger Properly
chapters.summary: Mirabel deciphers the ledger's structure: each child has two entries—one when 'kept,' one when 'taken.' Eleven children, ten pairs complete. Pip's second entry is blank. Beat: hope with teeth.

chapters.title: The House Appraises Back
chapters.summary: Mirabel realizes the survey metaphor literally: the house evaluates everyone who enters, measuring their worth as a keeper. His file, in his handwriting, grows daily. Beat: identity theme crystallizes—he was chosen because he counts things.

chapters.title: Odile's Letters
chapters.summary: In the county archive, Mirabel finds Odile's unsent letters: she discovered what lived below, refused to hand over children as 'payment,' and planned to seal them all inside together rather than surrender any. Beat: Odile becomes a mirror of Mirabel's choice.

chapters.title: What Was Taken in 1974
chapters.summary: The town took something that night—not just hid it. The fire brigade, the magistrate, the matron: all complicit in trading twelve lives for the town's prosperity. Beat: human evil worse than the ghost.

chapters.title: Pip
chapters.summary: Mirabel speaks aloud to the warm room. A voice answers through the walls—a child asking if he's come to take them or keep them. He answers honestly: he doesn't know yet. Beat: first contact; honesty as currency.

chapters.title: The Client's Visit
chapters.summary: The developer arrives, dismissive, and stands too long before Odile's portrait. That night his car won't start; his reflection lags. He fires Mirabel by phone. Beat: consequences of refusal; Mirabel freed from duty.

chapters.title: Free and Unmoored
chapters.summary: Jobless, Mirabel should leave. Instead he buys supplies, moves into the site trailer permanently. Danny covers for him. Beat: choosing the haunted place over the safe world—found family forming.

chapters.title: Tally Marks
chapters.summary: Danny's marks have multiplied; the house is counting him toward something. Mirabel teaches him the rituals—lights on, doors counted—and for the first time shares them with another person. Beat: intimacy through shared fear.

chapters.title: Below the Bolts
chapters.summary: Through the sealed door, knocking answers knocking. Mirabel and Danny map the rhythm: it matches the ledger's entries, one knock per name. Someone down there is still keeping count. Beat: the trapped are alive in some sense.

chapters.title: Reyes Speaks
chapters.summary: Reyes, recovered but hollowed, describes the cellar: rows of small beds, a woman reading aloud, a darkness at the far end that eats names. He remembers his own name going. Beat: horror of erasure—identity as food.

chapters.title: The Second Door
chapters.summary: Mirabel finds the interior side of the seal: a bolt thrown by hands inside, and beneath it, scratched small: HE COUNTS WRONG ON PURPOSE. Odile sabotaged the bargain. Beat: revelation—Odile cheated the thing below.

chapters.title: The Bargain Beneath
chapters.summary: Assembled history: the house stands on something older that trades keeping for taking. Every generation it offers a contract: give me some, and I'll hold the rest safe forever. Odile refused the terms. Beat: the true antagonist defined.

chapters.title: It Offers Me the Pen
chapters.summary: The ledger appears open, a pen laid across it, a fresh page headed with MIRABEL STERLING. Sign as keeper, and the children go free—all but one. The trade is always one. Beat: temptation made explicit.

chapters.title: Whose Name
chapters.summary: Mirabel nearly signs. The blank line waits. Pip's voice asks him not to choose anyone. Danny, watching, says he'd volunteer. Mirabel tears the page out. Beat: love against duty at full pressure.

chapters.title: The House Turns
chapters.summary: Refusal angers it. Doors multiply and mislead; the trailer floods with cellar air; Danny's tally marks bleed. The house stops courting and starts collecting. Beat: darkest hour begins.

chapters.title: Danny Taken
chapters.summary: Danny vanishes at the sealed door, leaving his hard hat and the ledger clutched in his jacket. Mirabel counts doors: forty-four. Beat: grief weaponized into resolve.

chapters.title: Reading Aloud
chapters.summary: Desperate, Mirabel tries the one ritual the house respects: he reads the ledger's names aloud at the sealed door. The knocking syncs to his voice. Somewhere below, a woman's voice joins his. Beat: recognition as power.

chapters.title: Odile's Side
chapters.summary: Through the stone, Mirabel and Odile converse across fifty years. She explains: the thing below cannot take what is truly seen and named—it can only hold the unnamed. Her mistake was hiding the children to protect them. Hiding fed it. Beat: thematic key turns.

chapters.title: Unsealing
chapters.summary: Mirabel gathers the town's descendants—including the old magistrate's daughter—and makes them witness. Together they read all eleven names, publicly, at the door. The bolts begin to draw back. Beat: communal reckoning; climax approaches.

chapters.title: The Cellar of Small Beds
chapters.summary: The door opens onto a preserved dormitory: eleven beds, warm lamplight, Odile aged not a day, the children shadows at the room's edge—and behind them, the dark thing, vast and patient, holding Danny. Beat: awe and horror fused.

chapters.title: The Trade Refused Again
chapters.summary: The thing offers the final terms: one name, freely given, and all others walk out. Danny steps forward. Mirabel steps in front of him and does neither—he instead reads Danny's name, Odile's, every child's, aloud, refusing the transaction entirely. Beat: climax; naming as defiance.

chapters.title: What Cannot Keep the Named
chapters.summary: Named and witnessed, the children come loose from the dark like moths from amber. The thing shrinks as recognition strips it, collapsing into the ledger itself. Odile closes the book. Beat: the monster undone by being seen.

chapters.title: Forty-One
chapters.summary: Dawn. The house has exactly forty doors again. Danny walks out squinting; the children's presence lingers as warmth and the smell of porridge. Odile's portrait smiles faintly. Beat: release; exhalation.

chapters.title: The Final Entry
chapters.summary: Mirabel writes the last ledger line himself: ALL KEPT, NONE TAKEN, HOUSE RELEASED. He certifies the true findings in his official report, ending his career of invisibility. Beat: identity reclaimed through truth-telling.

chapters.title: Found Family
chapters.summary: Weeks later: Danny and Mirabel share a flat above the archive where the ledger rests in public view. Reyes visits. The foundlings' names go on a memorial stone. Beat: warmth earned; love without transaction.

chapters.title: Portrait and Cellar
chapters.summary: Mirabel returns once to photograph Hollowmere before demolition. In the final frame, the cellar door stands open, empty, and the portrait's eyes look past him—at the reader. He leaves the lights on anyway. Beat: quiet coda; the habit of care remains.
